lines.original_literal: `psql` uses `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, but a shell escape needs an additional child-status check. The collector checks `SHELL_ERROR` immediately after `pg_dump`, and accepts success only when the exact completion marker appears after the final transaction close. Therefore an early `\quit` following a failed child cannot be mistaken for a successful capture. A SQL error, missing completion marker or unreadable dump also fails the operation. This follows the documented [`psql` shell-status and error behavior](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/app-psql.html).
lines.behavior: Historical psql ON_ERROR_STOP alone could miss child command failure; explicit SHELL_ERROR and terminal marker guard prevent false success of partial dump.
